rationale: Both alternatives have zero DRC violations and zero unconnected items, without schematic parity yet.
Any-net route avoids the added In2 V3V3 double-reference loss observed in the short candidate and adds no new fast-signal ground-loss projection in the reviewed layers.
Longer routing does not change board outline, wire-pad locations or intended case envelope.
Conditional copper-only series resistance to R37 is about 0.301 ohm versus about 0.194 ohm for the short candidate; this alone does not disqualify either path.
Select a working integration base to advance schematic/BOM/mechanics; do not treat this choice as validated PI, thermistor protection or a manufacturing release.
required_before_release: Synchronize film sensor interface and R13 package/MPN with schematic and BOM; rerun parity/ERC/DRC.
Review battery sensor R-T bounds, comparator common-mode limits and installed thermal lag.
Update board model and wire endpoints in case/assembly, qualify seller joining and strain relief.
Evaluate BAT_TS and both comparator thresholds during charging, USB transfers and memory writes; no false hot/cold release or oscillation.
Evaluate VBUS_LIMITED reference change with charger/input decoupling and grounding.
Confirm filled/capped via manufacture and actual battery harness fit.
limits: Declared resistivity scenario and nominal CAD copper geometry; not supplier worst-case process limits.
Vias treated as ideal; external wires, joints, contact and ground-return resistance excluded.
Each endpoint path is an isolated series-resistance sensitivity, not a full distributed circuit solution.
Beta sensitivity is approximate and does not bound the actual thermistor R-T curve.
No capacitance, inductive/capacitive pickup, comparator common-mode guarantees, leakage or PDN solution.
Longer path alone is not a rejection criterion; geometry/DRC alone is not acceptance.
